text: A major challenge for almost every online service is reliably identifying users and knowing whether a given user or agent can be trusted.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Historically, web services leaned on cookies stored in the browser to remember a visitor and recognize them when they return.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: The problem is that cookies live in the user's own browser and are easy to remove, block, or avoid entirely, so a bad actor can simply clear them to escape recognition.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: IP blocking and CAPTCHA puzzles are firmer approaches, but they can frustrate legitimate users while doing little to stop a determined attacker.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: That leaves developers stuck between being too lax in losing control or too strict in driving real users away.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Fingerprint.js was started in 2012 as an open source project.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: In 2019, Fingerprint was launched as a separate, full commercial platform built on the original Fingerprint.js GitHub library to recognize devices and browsers without relying on cookies.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: It handles identification by reading over 100 signals, from fonts and screen resolution to how a device renders audio and graphics.
speaker: SPEAKER_01
